description: Figure 3 is a set of three pie charts representing the problem distribution based on correctness under different knowledge settings. The three pie charts are labeled "easy", "medium", and "hard" and each is divided into four slices. The slices are labeled and colored according to a legend on the right side of the figure, with categories "N+K+", "N-K+", "N-K-", and "N+K-", represented by distinct colors, although the exact colors are not specified. The "easy" pie chart has slices representing approximately 9.8% "N+K+", 61.5% "N-K+", 34.6% "N-K-", and a small proportion of "N-K+" is not visible but can be inferred to be a small percentage. The "medium" pie chart has slices representing approximately 2.3% "N+K+", 65.4% "N-K+", 30.8% "N-K-", and a small proportion of "N+K-". The "hard" pie chart has slices representing approximately 4.7% "N+K+", 25.1% "N-K+", 30.6% "N-K-", and 39.6% "N+K-". Each pie chart includes percentage labels inside the slices. The slices are not visually emphasized or exploded. The pie charts are arranged in order of difficulty, from "easy" to "hard", and the proportions of the slices vary across the three charts.
